label: FIXTURE RESULT: pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation
symptom: Some customers say their transfers are failing or taking several seconds.

report.summary: After the 10:55:06 restart the pool was cut to 2 connections with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session held locks, so requests timed out on connections and returned 500/503.

findings.claim: The restart at 10:55:06 shrank the pool from 10 to 2 connections and the acquire timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config changed at the restart; the pool reports max 2 and 119 acquisition timeouts.

findings.claim: About 30% of transfers failed (55×500, 82×503) with p95 of 1.9 s, consistent with pool acquisition timeouts.
findings.reason: The 119 timeouts roughly match the 137 server errors; pending borrowers and active connections rose only in the post-restart window.

findings.claim: A non-app session idle in a transaction blocked two ledger_app sessions for about 2 s, holding the tiny pool's connections.
findings.reason: Sessions 84876 and 84877 waited on 84878 (idle in transaction) in 26-28 samples between 10:55:09 and 10:56:31.

findings.claim: The outbox delivery path is not the cause. All 330 attempts succeeded and the backlog was small; the dips in publications track the request failures.
findings.reason: 0 failed outbox rows, pending at most 4, delivery p95 76 ms (auth about 70 ms, handler under 0.1 ms).

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s, and the identity of the 'other' idle-in-transaction session is unknown.
Failures are not broken down by cause or time; the 500 and 503 split is not tied to specific causes.
next_checks: Identify session 84878 (its owner and query) and why it stayed idle in a transaction.
Restore the pool to 10 connections with a 30 s timeout and re-measure the transfer error rate.

alternatives.reason: Delivery totals are about 72 ms and every attempt succeeded; the outbox backlog stayed small.
alternatives.hypothesis: The slow consumer or auth step caused the slow transfers.

alternatives.reason: Both co-occur after the restart; the evidence cannot separate their contributions.
alternatives.hypothesis: The pool shrink alone, without the blocking session, caused the errors.

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 37 samples; 119 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: Transfer failures and slowness line up with a pool shrunk from 10 to 2 connections (timeout 250 ms) at the 10:55:06 restart, plus idle-in-transaction sessions holding locks. Outbox delivery looks healthy.

findings.claim: The restart at 10:55:06 cut poolMaximumSize from 10 to 2 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed values before and after the restart.

findings.claim: The tiny pool was exhausted: 119 acquisition timeouts, with pending borrowers and active connections peaking at the configured maximum of 2.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts, max pending 2 and max active 2 in the window after the restart.

findings.claim: The 500/503 errors (30% of transfers) and multi-second p95/p99 latency are likely from pool exhaustion and lock waits on sessions idle in transaction.
findings.reason: Server errors and slow requests coincide with pool saturation (10:55:18–10:56:23) and blocking from 10:55:09 to 10:56:31, max wait about 2 s.

alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox/consumer delivery problems cause the failures.
alternatives.reason: All 330 deliveries succeeded at about 72 ms, with no failed outbox rows and only 1-4 pending.

alternatives.hypothesis: Lock blocking by idle-in-transaction sessions is the primary cause, independent of the pool change.
alternatives.reason: The blocker session 84878 is not attributed to a code path, so its share versus pool exhaustion cannot be separated.

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s and pool gauges every 5 s, so brief events may be missed.
The restart makes counters span both sides; errors cannot be split before and after 10:55:06. 10 gauge samples were NaN.
next_checks: Identify what session 84878 (idle in transaction) is and why it holds locks.
Restore poolMaximumSize and the connection timeout, then compare transfer error ratio and latency.
